bit_field_value.@description: XADR fixed, no change at all
XADR increased by 1 after row. For READ operation, XADR increases by 1 after reading the last word of row. For PROG operation, XADR increases by 1 after NVSTR falls.
XADR increased for diagonal. For PROG-DIAGONAL operation, XADR is increased to create diagonal pattern.
XADR increased by sector. During ERASE operation, XADR increased by number of rows in a sector when NVSTR falls.
XADR inversed. XADR is inversed after reading one word or after programming one row when NVSTR falls.
XADR increased by 2 after row. For READ operation, XADR is increased by 2 after reading the last word of a row. For PROG operation, XADR is increased by 2 when NVSTR falls.
XADR[0] inversed. XADR[0] is inversed after reading one word or after programming one row when NVSTR falls.
XADR increased by 1. For READ operations only, XADR increased by 1 after each read cycle.
XADR decreased by 1 after row. For READ operations only, XADR is decreased by 1 after YADR decreases to 0.
XADR decreased by 1. For READ operations only, XADR is decreased by 1 after each read cycle.
YADR fixed, no change at all
YADR for ICKBD. For PROG and READ operations, YADR changed to generate inverse checkerboard pattern.
YADR for CKBD. For PROG and READ operations, YADR changed to generate checkerboard pattern.
YADR increased by 1. For READ operations, YADR increased by 1 after each read cycle. For PROG operations, YADR increased by 1 after YE falls.
YADR increased for diagonal. For PROG-DIAGONAL operation, YADR is increased to create diagonal pattern.
YADR inversed. YADR is inversed after reading one word or after programming one word when YE falls.
YADR[0] inversed. YADR[0] is inversed after reading one word or after programming one word when YE falls.
YADR increased by 1 after last row. For READ operations only, YADR is increased by 1 after XADR reaches last row.
YADR decreased by 1. For READ operations only, YADR is decreased by 1 after each read cycle.
YADR decreased by 1 after first row. For READ operations only, YADR is decreased by 1 after XADR decreases to 0.
CKBD pattern. For READ operations only, compare DOUT with checkerboard data pattern for each read cycle.
ICKBD pattern. For READ operations only, compare DOUT with inverse checkerboard data pattern for each read cycle.
Diagonal pattern. Used for READ operations only, compare DOUT to diagonal pattern.
Fixed data pattern. For READ operations, comparison to DOUT for selected groups; refer to R_ADR_CTRL[GRPSEL] for modules with multiple groups.

Random data pattern which will be generated based on the initial seed set in R_DATA; for READ operations, used for DOUT comparison of selected groups. For PROG operations, used to control DIN of selected groups.

DOUT based pattern. For READ operations only, DOUT of selected group will be latched in R_DATA. If more than one group is selected in R_ADR_CTRL[GRPSEL], the group with the lower index will be latched.

R_DATA based pattern. For READ operations, expected DOUT value of selected groups equals to R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0]. For PROG operations, DIN of selected groups equals R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0].
SCAN-IO pattern. For READ operations, control expected DOUT value of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern. For PROG operations, control DIN of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern.

REPAIR set. For PROG operation to IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 and R_REPAIR1_1 will control DIN. For READ operation on IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), DOUT will be compared against R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 andR_REPAIR1_1. When this option is selected, only one flash block can be selected.
REPAIR load. For READ operation only, DOUT from IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2) is loaded to R_REPAIR0 and R_REPAIR1.
